title: Split capacity snapshot merge and introduce ephemeral-node fastpath
creator: Maya Gupta
description:
Background: Over time the capacity planner has accumulated a large, single-step 'snapshot merge' routine that both consolidates leases and computes allocation deltas. This central merge is a frequent hot path during autoscaler reconciliation and is a major source of CPU spikes and long-tail reconcile latency. It also tightly couples lease state mutation with several housekeeping side effects (metrics emission, eviction annotations, and orphan reclamation), making targeted fixes risky and long-running.

Goal: Decompose the snapshot merge into two orthogonal components: a lightweight merge (fast-path) that produces a minimally-validated view suitable for making immediate placement/eviction decisions, and a deferred mutation pipeline that applies heavy side effects asynchronously. Introduce an ephemeral-node fastpath that bypasses several checks for short-lived preemptible nodes to dramatically shorten their reconcile cost. The work should reduce median autoscaler reconcile time by >=40% under mixed workloads and improve 99th percentile CPU usage during scale events.

Scope:
- Extract core snapshot merge logic into a pure, deterministic function with a clear input/output contract.
- Implement incremental validators (cheap first, expensive later) so the fast-path runs only cheap checks.
- Add an ephemeral-node tag and fastpath schedule to treat node leases <10m as low-trust but high-throughput for allocation decisions.
- Move metrics emission and eviction annotation into an asynchronous pipeline plumbed behind the deferred mutation queue.
- Add feature flags to gate fast-path and deferred mutation pipeline for safe rollouts.

Out of scope: full rewrite of capacity planner heuristics, changes to binding controller protocols, or new cluster lifecycle APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Fast-path merge function extracted and unit-tested with determinism property (stable outputs for same input)
Autoscaler reconcile median latency reduced by >=40% in benchmark harness for mixed allocation workloads
99th percentile CPU usage during simulated scale-up reduced by >=25%
Deferred mutation queue implemented and validated: side effects observable in logs/metrics within 30s of reconcile completion
Feature flags implemented and e2e rollout strategy documented in the rollout_plan
No regression in lease correctness: end-to-end allocation tests unchanged within tolerance thresholds
design_notes: Prefer pure functions for merge to allow fast unit testing and deterministic smoke-checks before side effects.
Fast-path must not mutate external state; it returns a reconciliation plan object that the mutation pipeline consumes.
Use a single-threaded, rate-limited worker pool for the deferred mutation pipeline to bound load on control plane components.
Ephemeral-node fastpath should be opt-in behind a feature flag and use a configurable TTL (default 10m).
Telemetry: add new metrics autoscaler.merge_fastpath.duration, autoscaler.deferred_mutations.queue_depth, autoscaler.fastpath.allocations.count
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable fastpath + deferred pipeline in staging clusters only; run benchmark harness and smoke tests (1 week).
Phase 2 (limited prod): Enable feature flag for 10% of autoscaler controllers; monitor reconcile latency, CPU, and allocation correctness (2 weeks).
Phase 3 (ramp): Gradually increase to 50% then 100% pending metrics; keep deferred queue in throttled mode during ramp.
Rollback: Flip feature flag off to return to single-step merge; deferred mutations will be drained by a fallback worker.
qa_tests: Unit tests for pure merge function covering edge cases (stale leases, overlapping reservations, orphan reclamation signals)
Integration test: simulate node churn and verify deferred mutations eventually applied and no allocation leak
Load test: run scaled benchmark harness with mixed small/large allocations and measure latency/cpu/alloc success rates
Chaos test: inject slow network to K8s apiserver and verify fastpath keeps reconcile bounded
